items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

The Associations Guide explains that build_association returns a new, unsaved object for a has_one association. However, it does not make clear that building this object replaces the association's current target and may immediately modify or destroy the existing persisted record.

This behavior is particularly surprising with dependent: :destroy, where calling build_association destroys the existing target before the newly built object is saved.

Related to #58732.

Detail

This Pull Request adds a warning to the has_one saving behavior documentation clarifying that:

  • the object returned by build_association remains unsaved;
  • building it replaces the current association target; and
  • Rails immediately removes a persisted target according to the association's :dependent option, including destroying it when dependent: :destroy is configured.

This is a documentation-only change and does not alter the existing Active Record behavior.

Additional information

No tests or CHANGELOG entry are needed because this change only clarifies existing documented behavior.

Motivation / Background

active_storage/vips only swallowed a LoadError whose message named libvips or ruby-vips. ruby-vips loads glib before libvips, so on a machine without libvips the error named glib-2.0 and the application failed to boot.

Fixes #58723

Detail

Treat every LoadError from requiring ruby-vips as ruby-vips being unavailable.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #58736. Ruby master prevents a worker Ractor from compiling a previously unseen non-strict template into a view context class that the main Ractor owns. That raises Ractor::IsolationError in the actual Action View rendering path.

Detail

Give Action View each worker Ractor its own empty-template-cache view context class. Controller-specific view context classes are also cached per Ractor, so their compiled method containers remain owned by the Ractor that performs template compilation.

The resolver regression now renders through a real Action View class created from a main-Ractor-owned frozen FileSystemResolver. It passes explicit frozen lookup details inside the worker to avoid unrelated I18n Ractor state.

Additional information

Manual validation on Ruby master:

  • Reproduced the reported isolation failure with the original test-only approach.
  • Ran a standalone render through a frozen FileSystemResolver and real Action View worker-Ractor class; it rendered "hello" and compiled into the worker-owned class.
  • Ran the two affected template test files 20 times in fresh processes without a failure.
  • Ran the targeted two-file Action View test command successfully: 58 runs, 176 assertions.
  • Ran the full Action View suite successfully: 3,292 runs, 7,449 assertions.
  • Ran RuboCop on all four changed files with no offenses.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why, including the related issue.
  • Tests are updated for the Ruby master regression.
  • CHANGELOG files are not needed for this minor compatibility bug fix.
items.title: Fix #58736: make Action View template compilation Ractor-local

items.content_html:
Follow-up to #58675

#58675 fixed db:prepare being silently skipped when extra flags (e.g.
-b 0.0.0.0, needed for Docker/Podman network binding) were passed to
bin/rails server, by checking the first two arguments instead of the
last two.

As @maxime-carbonneau pointed out on that PR, this broke the default
case: Rails 8+ apps include Thruster by default, and the generated
Dockerfile's CMD is ["./bin/thrust", "./bin/rails", "server"], not
["./bin/rails", "server"]. Checking the first two arguments assumes
./bin/rails is always first, which isn't true with Thruster in front
of it.

This check has actually flipped between first-two-args and
last-two-args once before in this file's history (7aaea30 →
11a93a0), each time trading one bug for the other. This PR replaces
the fixed-position check with one that scans the full argument list
for ./bin/rails immediately followed by server, wherever it
appears — correct regardless of a Thruster prefix, trailing flags,
both, or neither.

Tests

Replaced the previous test (which only pattern-matched the script's
source text) with one that actually executes the generated
bin/docker-entrypoint against real invocation shapes — plain, with
flags, behind Thruster, behind Thruster with flags — plus a negative
case confirming unrelated commands don't trigger db:prepare.
items.title: Fix docker-entrypoint to detect bin/rails server behind Thruster too

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Since cd0a258 (released in 8.1.3.1), loading active_storage/vips at boot raised whenever ruby-vips was installed but libvips or ruby-vips was too old to block the unfuzzed loaders. That stopped :mini_magick applications from booting even though Active Storage never hands them content through libvips.

Fixes #58394.

Detail

Keep loading ruby-vips and calling Vips.block_untrusted(true) at boot for every processor, and raise only where libvips is used: when the Vips transformer loads, and when the Vips analyzer reads an image. For :vips applications the error still fires during boot, now from after_initialize rather than engine load.

Additional information

This is an alternative to #58406, which moves the require out of boot and so drops the boot-time block for every processor other than :vips. A CHANGELOG entry is included. Reproduced with a demo app pinning ruby-vips 2.1.4 and variant_processor = :mini_magick: 8.1.3.1 and main fail to boot, this branch boots.

items.content_html:
… same record within MySQL transactions.

Motivation / Background

Fixes #54281

  1. find_or_create_by delegates to create_or_find_by in Rails 8.
  2. The loser's savepointed INSERT hits 1062 Duplicate entry, and InnoDB leaves it holding a shared lock on the duplicate index record.
  3. create_or_find_by sees an open transaction and re-reads with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
  4. Two or more losers each hold S and each request X, so they deadlock (1213) and the transaction rolls back.

This Pull Request has been created to remove this source of deadlocks from a method that is meant to be able to be safely run concurrently.

Detail

This PR fixes a MySQL deadlock in concurrent find_or_create_by and create_or_find_by calls, including their bang variants, by using a shared lock when reading back a record after a duplicate insert. The shared lock preserves visibility under REPEATABLE READ while avoiding the competing shared-to-exclusive lock upgrades caused by FOR UPDATE. The tradeoff is that callers can now return the same record concurrently; if they subsequently update it within their transactions, they can deadlock on the later lock upgrade, where an exclusive readback could have serialized them earlier.

Additional information

Regression tests cover both isolation levels, secondary unique indexes, and nested savepoints, with verification on MySQL 8.4, MySQL 5.7, and MariaDB through both adapters.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Allow callers to limit concurrency for specific async query workloads without changing executor configuration, as discussed in this proposal.

Detail

Add ActiveRecord.with_async_query_execution_limit(limit) for load_async and async_* methods. The limit is shared across connection pools in the current execution context.

Unlike the original proposal’s non-blocking scheduling, calls wait for capacity before checking out a connection.

The limit must be a positive integer, and limit blocks cannot be nested.

Queries made inside with_connection using the same connection pool are not limited. For example, Post.async_count inside Post.with_connection bypasses the limit to avoid waiting while holding a database connection.

Additional information

Motivation / Background

Browsers and password managers use this well-known URL to send people straight to a site's change password page, typically after warning them that a saved password appeared in a breach.

Detail

This Pull Request a new route on the authentication generator for a well-known URL. The route is a temporary redirect, as the specification requires the well-known URL not host the page itself.

get "/.well-known/change-password", to: redirect("/passwords/new", status: 302)

API-only applications skip the route, since they generate no pages to redirect to.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

structure_dump builds its --ignore-table/-T exclusions by matching schema_ignored_tables against ActiveRecord::Base's current connection, not the database being dumped, and then prefixes the target database's name onto the result.

In a multi-database application that is wrong in both directions. Reproduced against MySQL with schema_ignored_tables = [/\A_.+_gho\z/], ActiveRecord::Base connected to one database while dumping another:

ambient connection database: activerecord_unittest
dumping: activerecord_unittest2
emitted: ["--ignore-table=activerecord_unittest2._lives_in_primary_gho"]

_lives_in_primary_gho exists in target? NO
_lives_in_target_gho  exists in target? YES

The false positive is harmless — the dump commands ignore unknown table names. The false negative is the bug: _lives_in_target_gho matches the patterns and really is in the dumped database, but is never excluded, so it ends up in the committed structure.sql. schema_ignored_tables silently does nothing for every database except whichever one ActiveRecord::Base happens to be connected to.

All three adapters that support :sql dumps shared the lookup. PostgreSQL has a second symptom from the same cause: it appends SET search_path TO #{connection.schema_search_path} to the dump, so dumping a non-primary database writes the primary's search path into that database's structure.sql.

structure_dump is also the only one of these tasks that never established a connection — create, drop and purge all do before touching connection.

Detail

The table list is now read from a connection to the dumped db_config, opened through db_config.new_connection and closed when the dump is done.

MySQL and SQLite only open it inside the schema_ignored_tables.any? branch, so with the default empty list they still shell out without connecting at all — no new reachability requirement for the common case. PostgreSQL already read a connection unconditionally for the search path, so it always opens one; what changes there is which database it connects to.

db_config.new_connection is used rather than DatabaseTasks.with_temporary_connection because the latter re-establishes ActiveRecord::Base's connection as a side effect of a dump, and leaves the connection open — on SQLite that recreated a database file after it had been deleted.

Additional information

Each adapter's regression test fails without the fix:

  • SQLite creates the ignored tables in the database being dumped, so only a connection to it can find them.
  • MySQL asserts the excluded table comes from the dumped config while a matching table in the ambient connection is left alone.
  • PostgreSQL asserts the dump gets the dumped database's search path: without the fix it reports Expected "statement\nSET search_path TO ambient_schema;\n\n" to include "SET search_path TO dumped_schema;".

The existing structure_dump tests in the PostgreSQL suite are wrapped in a helper that fakes the dumped database's connection, since two of them configure an unreachable host on purpose. The helper also asserts the connection is closed.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

A SyntaxError with a multi-line message breaks the debug error page in development.

ActiveSupport::SyntaxErrorProxy turns the lines of a syntax error message into backtrace entries so the error page can show the source location of the error, and it treats every message line as a trace entry. Prose lines then flow into ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper's source extraction, which resolves them as paths against Rails.root.

When such a path names a directory, File.exist? passes and reading it raises Errno::EISDIR in the middle of rendering the error page, so the browser gets the public 500 page instead.

I ran into this while working on #58721.

Detail

SyntaxErrorProxy#parse_message_for_trace now only treats message lines containing a :<line> location as trace entries. ExceptionWrapper#source_fragment now checks File.file? instead of File.exist? before reading a source fragment.

Additional information

Herb's compile errors are SyntaxError subclasses that report several template errors in one message, but the bug is independent of any template engine.

The reason why Herb uses multi-line exception messages is because there is no other structured way to report syntax errors for views. I wonder if we are missing a better way to report errors in a more structured way.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

AbstractTasks#run_cmd_error echoes back the command that failed, and MySQL's structure_dump/structure_load pass --password=<value> on the command line. So any failure of those tasks prints the database password:

failed to execute:
mysqldump --user=pat --password=wossname --result-file structure.sql --no-data ...

Under CI that writes the password into the build log, where it persists.

dbconsole already avoids this deliberately, emitting a bare -p unless include_password is set. The tasks path had no equivalent guard.

Detail

--password=<value> is now replaced with --password=[FILTERED] in the message. The filtering happens where the message is built rather than in the MySQL tasks, so it covers any command given a --password argument.

PostgreSQL passes its password through PGPASSWORD in the environment and SQLite has none, so MySQL is the only adapter affected today.

Additional information

This is about what gets written to logs and stdout. The password is still visible to other local processes in ps output while the command runs, which is a separate, pre-existing concern and not addressed here.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

dbconsole and structure_dump/structure_load build their command-line flags from a key map that only lists mysql2's SSL option spellings (sslca, sslcapath, sslcert, sslcipher, sslkey), so Trilogy's underscored spellings (ssl_ca, ssl_capath, ...) never reach mysql or mysqldump.

Both drivers spell ssl_mode identically, which makes the failure loud rather than silent. An app on Trilogy configured with ssl_mode: verify_ca and ssl_ca connects fine, but mysqldump receives --ssl-mode=verify_ca without the CA that satisfies it:

mysqldump: Got error: 2026: SSL connection error: CA certificate is required
if ssl-mode is VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_IDENTITY when trying to connect

Spelling it sslca instead is not a workaround. Neither adapter translates config keys, and a key a driver does not recognize is ignored rather than rejected, so sslca configures nothing on Trilogy. Against MySQL 8.0 with ssl_mode: VERIFY_CA and a CA path that does not exist (trilogy 2.12.5):

base = { host: "127.0.0.1", username: "root", ssl_mode: Trilogy::SSL_VERIFY_CA }

Trilogy.new(base.merge(ssl_ca: "/does/not/exist.pem"))
# => Trilogy::SyscallError::ENOENT: No such file or directory - trilogy_ssl_upgrade

Trilogy.new(base.merge(sslca: "/does/not/exist.pem"))
# => Trilogy::SSLError: trilogy_ssl_upgrade: SSL Error: certificate verify failed

ssl_ca makes trilogy open the file; sslca verifies against the default trust store instead, showing the key was dropped and the connection fell back to the system CAs.

Detail

The whole mapping now lives in one cli_arg_map class attribute on AbstractMysqlAdapter, and both call sites read it from the adapter rather than keeping their own inline copy, so the commands are configured by the same values as the connection.

TrilogyAdapter amends that map with the option names trilogy accepts, plus ssl_crl and ssl_crlpath, which trilogy supports and mysql2 has no equivalent for.

One behavior change: an option spelled for the other driver is no longer passed along, so sslca on Trilogy no longer produces --ssl-ca. That configuration never configured the connection either. Two Trilogy tests asserted the old behavior and are updated; the mysql2 tests are unchanged.

Additional information

Verified end to end against MySQL 8.0.46. With ssl_mode: VERIFY_CA and ssl_ca set, a :sql format structure dump fails on main with the error above and succeeds with this change.

trilogy interns exactly these option names in ext/trilogy-ruby/cext.c: ssl_ca, ssl_capath, ssl_cert, ssl_cipher, ssl_crl, ssl_crlpath, ssl_key, ssl_mode. mysql2 reads sslkey, sslcert, sslca, sslcapath and sslcipher in Mysql2::Client#ssl_set.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because the methods generated by has_rich_text could not be overridden and composed with super. has_rich_text :content defines content, content= and content? with class_eval directly on the model, so an override in the same class replaces the generated implementation and there is no way to call back into it:

class Message < ApplicationRecord
  has_rich_text :content

  def content=(body)
    super(body&.strip) # NoMethodError: super: no superclass method 'content='
  end
end

Detail

This Pull Request changes the three class_eval calls in ActionText::Attribute#has_rich_text to generated_association_methods.class_eval, so the reader, the writer and the predicate are defined in a module included in the model instead of on the model itself. Overriding any of them in the class body and calling super now works, matching has_one_attached.

Both writer variants are covered, so the change applies with store_if_blank: true and store_if_blank: false.

Tests were added to actiontext/test/unit/model_test.rb, following the style of the Active Storage tests in activestorage/test/models/attached/one_test.rb.

Additional information

Active Storage had the same problem and fixed it in #32921 by generating has_one_attached and has_many_attached methods in the model's GeneratedAssociationMethods module. This applies the same fix to Action Text.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Pull Request #58552 added Herb to Action View as an ERB implementation with no way to select it. This pull request is the follow-up discussed there and adds the framework default that enables Herb for HTML templates.

Detail

Adds config.action_view.html_erb_implementation to select the ERB implementation for templates with the HTML format. The :herb option compiles them through ERB::Herb, and :erubi keeps them on erb_implementation like every other template format.

The 8.2 framework defaults set :herb, so new applications and applications running config.load_defaults 8.2 compile their HTML templates through Herb. All other template formats, keep compiling through Erubi.

Applications that cannot immediately migrate their templates set the option back using:

Rails.application.config.action_view.html_erb_implementation = :erubi

Additional information

Setting :erubi falls through to erb_implementation instead of forcing ERB::Erubi, so an application with a custom ERB implementation keeps it for HTML templates too. Any other value raises an ArgumentError at boot.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Inside with_local_cache, read_multi returns the local cache hits first rather than following the requested order:

cache.read_multi("a", "b", "c").keys   # => ["b", "a", "c"], when only "b" was a local hit

0f231b0 fixed exactly this for fetch_multi. read_multi_entries sits two methods below, builds its result the same way (local hits, then merge! of whatever the store returns) and was left behind.

Detail

Slices the result by the requested names, as fetch_multi does.

Keys that were not found stay absent rather than being filled in with nil, since slice only keeps keys the hash already has. That matters here because read_multi may legitimately return fewer keys than requested.

items.content_html:
Fixes #58715.

try_to_queue_for_background_connection waited up to a hardcoded 100 seconds for a connection tied up in background maintenance, ignoring the pool's own checkout_timeout. Now it's bounded by checkout_timeout instead.

Scoped narrowly to that one bug. There's a second, more debatable question raised in the same discussion (#54175) -- whether checkout should prefer opening a new connection over queueing at all when the pool has room to grow -- but that's a deliberate design choice defended by an existing test and comment (test_checkout_queues_behind_maintenance_connections), so I left it alone here.

Added a test that pins a connection in maintenance indefinitely and confirms checkout raises ConnectionTimeoutError within the configured checkout_timeout rather than hanging.
items.title: Bound background-maintenance checkout wait to checkout_timeout

items.content_html:
Fixes #58713.

configuration_hash[:keepalive] || 600 treats a literal keepalive: false the same as the key being absent, since false is falsy in Ruby — so keepalive: false silently falls back to the default 600s instead of disabling it.

Uses fetch to distinguish "absent" from "explicitly false", and keeps nil/true mapping to the 600s default so existing behavior for those is unchanged. keepalive: 0 still disables it too, matching the current documented way to turn it off.

Added tests for keepalive: false and keepalive: 0.
items.title: Fix keepalive: false being ignored in database.yml

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

SQLite does not allow PRAGMA foreign_keys to be changed while a transaction is active.
Although the SQLite adapter disables referential integrity before rebuilding a table,
ActiveRecord::Migrator has already opened an outer DDL transaction by that point.
Consequently, disabling foreign keys is a no-op and dropping the original table during
reconstruction can trigger ON DELETE CASCADE, silently deleting rows from referencing
tables.

Fixes #58705.

Detail

This pull request introduces an adapter hook for migration transactions. The default
implementation preserves the existing transaction behavior, while SQLite overrides the
hook to disable referential integrity before opening the migration transaction and restore
it afterward.

The regression test runs the schema change through MigrationContext, verifies that
referencing rows survive the table reconstruction, and confirms that foreign key
enforcement and cascading deletes still work after the migration completes.

  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this pull request fixes a related issue, include it in the commit message.
  • Tests are added or updated for the bug fix.
  • The Active Record changelog is updated.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #53683.

Non-digested public files (robots.txt, favicons, 404.html, etc.) currently get the same far-future Cache-Control as digest-stamped assets because the production generator sets a single 1-year header for everything.

A previous attempt (#55249) put a path-based lambda in public_file_server.headers, but Rack::Files stringifies Proc values, producing Cache-Control: #<Proc:…> (#55617). That change was reverted in #55633.

Detail

  1. ActionDispatch::FileHandler resolves header values that respond_to?(:call) per request (path, env) and merges them onto the response. Only non-callable headers are passed into Rack::Files, so callables are never stringified.
  2. Production generator template restores path-based caching:
    • /assets/* → public, immutable, max-age=1.year
    • everything else → public, max-age=1.day

Additional information

  • Tests cover callable headers in actionpack/test/dispatch/static_test.rb and railties/test/application/middleware/static_test.rb.
  • Existing string-header configuration is unchanged.
items.title: Fix public file Cache-Control for non-digested assets

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

config.active_storage.streaming_max_ranges is documented in the configuring guide, but setting it does nothing:

config.active_storage.streaming_max_ranges = 5
ActiveStorage.streaming_max_ranges # => 1

The setting was added with the multi-range limit in bb78f8c, along with the guide entry, but the active_storage.configs initializer never copied it into ActiveStorage.streaming_max_ranges. The guide says "If you need multiple byte range support, you can increase that setting", which is not possible today.

Detail

Copies the value in the initializer, next to the fifteen settings already handled there.

Since the config was inert, an application that needed a higher limit had to assign ActiveStorage.streaming_max_ranges in an initializer. That assignment is now overwritten on boot, so the CHANGELOG entry points those applications at the config option.

  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
